samples.summary: Healing to `currentId = undefined` on an empty deck is a permanent dead end — the cursor is never re-seeded when slides come back (e.g. undoing the delete that emptied the deck), leaving a blank canvas.
samples.evidence: `resolveCurrentSlide` starts with `if (id === undefined) return undefined;` (line 1540) and the empty-deck heal sets `this.currentId = next?.id` → `undefined` (line 1561). After that no code path re-seeds the cursor: the only places that set `currentId` are the constructor (line 1022), `setCurrentSlide` (1512, driven by user/thumbnail action) and `setStore` (1635). So once a peer (or a local `removeSlides` of the last slide) empties the deck, an undo/redo or a peer re-adding a slide restores `doc.slides` but `currentId` stays `undefined` and both `render()` and `repaintOverlay()` keep taking the `!slide` branch — the canvas stays blank until the user clicks a thumbnail. Note this is a regression relative to the old behaviour, where the dangling id started matching again as soon as the slide was restored. The new test at current-slide-heal.test.ts asserts `getCurrentSlideId()` is undefined and that `store.undo()` restores the slide, but never asserts the cursor recovers. A `doc.slides.length > 0 && id === undefined → slides[0]` re-seed (or not nulling the id) is what is missing.

samples.summary: The heal cancels (discards) an in-flight text edit without checking that the edit is anchored to the slide that actually vanished — an edit on a still-existing slide can be thrown away.
samples.evidence: `if (this.editingElementId !== null) this.exitEditMode('cancel');` discards unconditionally. But the edit's slide is snapshotted at entry (`enterEditMode`'s own comment at line 4137: "We snapshot the slide id at enter-time because the user could have switched slides during editing") and `setCurrentSlide` (1504–1517) exits a crop session but deliberately does NOT exit text editing. So `editingElementId` can belong to slide A while `currentId` is slide B; when B is removed, the heal discards the user's unsaved typing on A instead of committing it. The crop path is safe (setCurrentSlide commits crops, and `cropSession.slideId` is always the current slide) — the text path has no equivalent guarantee and no `slideId` comparison. Low confidence only because the document-level pointerdown at 3845 commits on most slide-switch gestures; the fix is to compare the edit's snapshotted slideId with the removed id.

samples.summary: `currentIndex` is only maintained inside `resolveCurrentSlide`; `setCurrentSlide` and `setStore` change `currentId` without it, so a heal can use an index that belongs to a different array and land the cursor on an unrelated slide.
samples.evidence: `setCurrentSlide` (1512) sets `this.currentId = id` and leaves `currentIndex` at whatever the last resolve produced — it happens to be refreshed because the method then calls `render()`/`repaintOverlay()`, but the invariant is not enforced (and `setCurrentSlide` does not validate that `id` exists, so a caller passing a stale id heals against the *previous* slide's index). Worse, `setStore` (1635-1638) swaps the whole document and assigns `currentId` from the new store without resetting `currentIndex`, so a heal in the swapped store (`LayoutEditStore`) uses an index from the old deck. `Math.min(...)` only clamps it into range; it does not make it meaningful. Setting `currentIndex` alongside every `currentId` write (or deriving it lazily) removes the class of bug.

samples.summary: The heal's teardown is incomplete: drill-in scope, hover highlight, pending guide/connector chrome and any in-flight drag/insert gesture stay anchored to the removed slide.
samples.evidence: Lines 1568-1571 tear down crop, text edit, cell selection and selection ids only. `Selection.clear()` (selection.ts:93) clears `ids` but leaves `scope_` — so after the heal the editor is still "drilled into" a group that lives on a deleted slide, and `repaintOverlay` keeps calling `toWorldFrame(..., scope, slide)` / `groupOverlayFrames(slide, ids, scope)` with that stale chain. Likewise `hoverHighlightId`, `pendingGuide`, `connectorCursor`, `paintSnapshot` and the pointer-drag sessions that snapshot `startSlide` (e.g. lines 5265, 5730, 6069) are untouched, so a gesture in flight when a peer deletes the slide will still try to commit against the removed slide id on pointerup. The comment ("Anything anchored to the removed slide has nowhere left to commit, so it is discarded") over-claims relative to what the code actually resets.

samples.summary: The new `editingCancel` escape hatch is not used by `detach()`, which is the other teardown that flushes a final `onCommit` — editor unmount still performs the store write (and phantom undo entry) the field's doc comment describes.
samples.evidence: `detach()` (2737) calls `this.editingTextBox.detach()` directly at 2744, bypassing both `exitEditMode('cancel')` and `finishEditMode()`. Per the new field comment at 852-865 (and the test's `mockMountTextBoxFlushing` mirroring `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts`), `detach()` synchronously flushes `onCommit` for a still-focused box, so unmounting the view mid-edit writes through `store.batch()` — pushing an undo entry and clearing redo — exactly the behaviour the diff calls out as wrong on the heal path. It also leaves `this.editingCancel` non-null after teardown (never reset in `detach`). If the unmount write is intentional (commit-on-unmount) it should be spelled `exitEditMode('commit')`.
searchedFor: grep exitEditMode|exitImageCrop call sites in editor.ts

samples.summary: When the heal empties the cursor, `render()` returns without clearing the canvas, so the deleted slide's pixels stay on screen.
samples.evidence: `if (!slide) { this.paintRuler(); return; }` (1441-1444) never clears the canvas. Previously an emptied deck also hit this branch via the dangling id, so this is not new, but the heal now makes `slide === undefined` a routine outcome of a peer delete/undo mid-session while the last painted frame remains visible under an empty overlay (repaintOverlay does paint an empty overlay, the canvas does not get cleared).

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. resolveCurrentSlide returns early when `currentId === undefined` (editor.ts:1540), and the empty-deck heal sets `this.currentId = next?.id` → undefined (editor.ts:1561). The only other writers to `currentId` are the constructor (editor.ts:1022), the public `setCurrentSlide` (editor.ts:1512, user/thumbnail/keyboard driven) and `setStore` (editor.ts:1635, reachable only from enter/exitLayoutEditMode at editor.ts:1645-1653); grep over packages/slides/src found no re-seed site. Both render() (editor.ts:1441-1444) and repaintOverlay() (editor.ts:1083-1093) take the `!slide` bail-out branch, so the canvas stays blank. The empty-deck state is reachable: the last-slide gate is local-only (thumbnail-panel.ts:301) while the store's removeSlides is unguarded, and the new test itself drives that state (current-slide-heal.test.ts:311-336) without asserting cursor recovery. No host-side recovery exists on desktop: slides-view.tsx:644-649 seeds a slide only once at mount before initializeEditor (line 658), and its sole onCurrentSlideChange use (line 1094) only broadcasts presence; a read-only mount deliberately skips the seed (slides-view.tsx:640-644), so a slide arriving later never paints. Mobile's independent sync (mobile-slides-view.tsx:183-191, 451-458) does not cover this path. Real logic bug in the correctness lane: blank canvas / broken core flow after undo or peer re-add until the user clicks a thumbnail.

finding.summary: Heal's `exitEditMode('cancel')` still flushes a store write (detach commits), so it writes during render() and drops the redo stack
finding.evidence: resolveCurrentSlide calls `this.exitEditMode('cancel')` under the comment "discarded rather than committed". But exitEditMode('cancel') → finishEditMode() → tb.detach() → docs `api.detach()`, which at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:940 does `if (focused && !committedOnce) { ... opts.onCommit?.(...) }` — a final commit flush. That routes into editor.ts:4117 `onCommit`, whose `cancelled` flag is only set by the docs Escape path, so `this.options.store.batch(() => store.withTextElement(slideId, ...))` runs with the slideId of the just-removed slide. Two consequences: (a) a store mutation is performed from inside `render()`, which is itself invoked synchronously from the store's own change notification (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1053); (b) MemSlidesStore.batch pushes an undo snapshot and does `this.redoStack = []` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1791-1792) *before* running fn, so even though the write then throws (caught and swallowed at editor.ts:4159), the redo entry for the just-undone `Add slide` is destroyed and a no-op undo entry is added. Yorkie's history behaves the same way (a new local change after undo clears redo). Reachable when a text edit is active while the current slide disappears: a peer deleting the slide, or the toolbar undo button (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/global-controls.tsx:55 calls store.undo() directly) while the in-place editor still holds focus.

verdict.reason: The finding's central premise is false in this repository. It claims onCommit's `cancelled` flag "is only set by the docs Escape path", so `exitEditMode('cancel')` -> `finishEditMode()` -> `tb.detach()` would flush a real store write. In fact `exitEditMode('cancel')` explicitly calls `this.editingCancel?.()` BEFORE `finishEditMode()` (editor.ts:4362-4368), and `editingCancel` (installed at editor.ts:4192-4194) sets the same closure variable `cancelled` (declared editor.ts:4065) that `onCancel` sets. So by the time `finishEditMode` (editor.ts:4604-4616) calls `tb.detach()` and docs flushes its final onCommit, the `if (!cancelled)` guard at editor.ts:4139 is false and `store.batch(...)` at editor.ts:4141 never executes: no write from inside render(), no undo snapshot, no redo-stack clear. `finishEditMode` nulls the `editingCancel` field at editor.ts:4607, but the flag already lives in the closure so that is irrelevant. The field doc comment at editor.ts:854-866 documents this exact hazard and states the setter exists so that `exitEditMode('cancel')` "mean[s] what it says". Both reachability paths the reviewer cites (peer delete, toolbar undo while editing) route through the same guarded `exitEditMode('cancel')` at editor.ts:1569, and `exitEditMode` returns early at editor.ts:4354 when no box is mounted, so there is no bypassing call site.

mergedFrom.summary: Teardown condition (`editingElementId !== null`) does not match `exitEditMode`'s own guard (`editingTextBox === null` early-return), so a divergent state leaves the editor wedged in a phantom edit

finding.summary: Empty-deck early return skips the whole teardown, leaving a live text-box editor / crop session anchored to a slide that no longer exists
finding.evidence: `if (doc.slides.length === 0) return undefined;` returns *before* `exitImageCrop(false)` / `exitEditMode('cancel')` / `setCellSelection(null)` / `selection.clear()` (lines 1550-1553). So when the removal that vanished the current slide also empties the deck, `currentId` stays dangling AND the mounted text box stays in the overlay with `editingElementId` non-null, and `cropSession` stays installed (its document-level keydown capture handler included, see finishCropSession at 2514). `render()` then bails at line 1428/1430 so the canvas is blank while a fully interactive text box floats over it; a subsequent commit from that box targets the removed slide id and throws out of the store (`MemSlidesStore.requireSlideIndex`). The local thumbnail path blocks a deck wipe (thumbnail-panel.ts:301), but two peers deleting disjoint halves concurrently, or an undo that removes the last slide, reaches slides.length === 0. The teardown block should run for the empty-deck case too (only the cursor move has no target).

verdict.reason: The quoted code does not exist. The finding claims `resolveCurrentSlide` contains `if (doc.slides.length === 0) return undefined;` ahead of the teardown, but editor.ts:1551-1555 instead computes `const empty = doc.slides.length === 0;` and uses it only to skip the cursor *move* (`next = empty ? undefined : doc.slides[nextIdx]`). There is no early return: editor.ts:1561-1562 sets `this.currentId = next?.id`, so on an empty deck currentId becomes undefined rather than dangling, and editor.ts:1568-1572 unconditionally runs the full teardown — `exitImageCrop(false)`, `exitEditMode('cancel')`, `setCellSelection(null)`, `selection.clear()`, plus the currentSlideListeners notification — for the empty-deck case as well. The in-tree comment at editor.ts:1546-1550 explicitly documents this choice for the peer-empties-the-deck scenario and names returning early as the rejected alternative, i.e. the finding describes the code that was deliberately not written. The only early return is editor.ts:1540 for an unset `currentId`, where there is no dangling id and no slide-anchored session. render() calls the resolver at editor.ts:1440 before bailing at 1441-1444, so the teardown does execute on the cited render path. No live text box or crop session can survive an emptied deck, so the described dangling-commit crash cannot occur.
